unaddressed_comments.author: shrutisinghania
unaddressed_comments.body: Nit: existing tests in this file still use literal `1024` (e.g. `createRange(/* offset= */ 1024, ...)` and `.setMaxMergeSize(1024)`), and using `KB` as an arbitrary seek offset in `strategy.position(KB)` reads a bit oddly. Either use `KB` consistently across the file or keep literals where the value isn't representing a byte-size unit.

unaddressed_comments.author: shrutisinghania
unaddressed_comments.body:
Returning `0` on an in-bounds read into a non-empty buffer violates the `ReadableByteChannel` contract for blocking channels and will spin callers like `SmallObjectOptimizer.ensureCached` and `GcsFooterOptimizer` (which loop `while (buffer.hasRemaining()) { if (source.read(buffer) == -1) ... }`).

Locking this in as expected behavior via a unit test will make fixing `readBytesFromSession` (to return `-1` or throw on an unexpected 0-byte response) look like a regression. Could we either drop this test and file an issue for the empty-payload handling, or add a `// TODO` comment noting that this documents current behavior pending a fix?

unaddressed_comments.author: shrutisinghania
unaddressed_comments.body: Nit: the anonymous `ReadStrategy.getLimit()` unconditionally returns `0`, so asserting `getLimit() == 0` after `position(...)` doesn't actually verify `position()`. Since both methods are no-op stubs on the dummy strategy, consider renaming to `createReadStrategy_positionAndGetLimit_areNoOps` so the test name doesn't imply a real state relationship between the two.

unaddressed_comments.author: shrutisinghania
unaddressed_comments.body: There are ~10 earlier `read_*` / `size_*` tests in this file that inline this same 3-line setup (and don't close the channel in try-with-resources). Worth a quick pass to reuse this helper there too.
